extraction.name: ACL OCL
extraction.description: A scholarly corpus derived from the ACL Anthology for open scientific research in computational linguistics. It includes metadata, PDF files, citation graphs, structured full texts with sections, figures, and links to Semantic Scholar, spanning 73K papers and 210K figures.
extraction.creator: Shaurya Rohatgi; Yanxia Qin; Benjamin Aw; Niranjana Unnithan; Min-Yen Kan
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The corpus was constructed by crawling PDF files and metadata from the ACL Anthology website, removing PDFs longer than 50 pages, extracting structured full text from PDFs with GROBID, extracting figures/tables with PDFFigures, and enriching records with Semantic Scholar Graph API data. The dataset is updated annually by downloading newly added ACL Anthology papers identified via URL changes.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw/source data consisted of ACL Anthology PDF documents and metadata from its website; these PDFs were used for full-text extraction, and additional external information was fetched from the Semantic Scholar Academic Graph API.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: Papers published from 1952 to September 2022; annual updates thereafter for newly added ACL Anthology papers.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Topic labels were created using a supervised neural/PLM-based topic classification model trained on a subset of 2,545 scientific papers with ground-truth topic labels, and the model predictions were extrapolated as silver-labeled topic information.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper states that it validates the importance of supervised data in topic classification.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: A pre-trained language model (PLM)-based topic classification method was used to generate silver topic labels; a public language detection toolkit was also used to automatically detect document language.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The corpus is biased toward peer-reviewed, open-access computational linguistics papers from the ACL Anthology, excluding other sources and potentially underrepresenting some topics.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited in scope to ACL Anthology papers, is not comprehensive, may have lower full-text extraction quality due to reliance on open-source PDF-to-text tools, has extraction failures especially for papers from 2000 to 2015, and is unlabeled for task-specific annotations.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is intended to support open scientific research, reproducibility, and analysis of trends in computational linguistics, including drawing attention to emerging and underrepresented topics such as Ethics of NLP.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Author information is included as metadata via linked knowledge graph records.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The corpus is designed to assist open scientific research in computational linguistics, support reproducibility, enable trend and topic analysis, and benefit existing research tasks through structured full texts, metadata, citation graphs, and figures.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors plan to maintain data currency by updating the corpus yearly to keep it aligned with ACL Anthology data, with a longer-term goal of hosting the data and extraction APIs on ACL Anthology itself.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Crawled PDFs and metadata from ACL Anthology, removed PDF files longer than 50 pages, extracted full text from PDFs using GROBID into the S2ORC-JSON schema, and automatically detected document language from title and abstract.

name.evidence: We present ACL OCL, a scholarly corpus derived from the ACL Anthology

description.evidence: We present ACL OCL, a scholarly corpus derived from the ACL Anthology to assist Open scientific research in the Computational Linguistics domain. Integrating and enhancing the previous versions of the ACL Anthology, the ACL OCL contributes metadata, PDF files, citation graphs and additional structured full texts with sections, figures, and links to a large knowledge resource (Semantic Scholar). The ACL OCL spans seven decades, containing 73K papers, alongside 210K figures.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: The OCL corpus is a small-scale collection of documents specifically focusing on peer-reviewed and open-access CL papers. As a result, it is not a comprehensive corpus like S2ORC (Lo et al., 2020), since it does not include any other sources beyond the ACL Anthology.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: it is not a comprehensive corpus like S2ORC... since it does not include any other sources beyond the ACL Anthology... only open-source toolkits are considered, although it is acknowledged that some paid PDF2text services might yield higher-quality full texts... We observe that our full-text extraction fail mostly for papers between the years 2000 to 2015... The OCL corpus is an unlabeled resource, lacking annotations for specific tasks that require labels.

rai:dataSocialImpact.evidence: Building scholarly corpora for open research accelerates scientific progress and promotes reproducibility in research... By analyzing the topics’ popularity, we ask for more attention on the emerging new topics such as “Ethics of NLP” and the declining underrepresented topics like “Discourse and Pragmatics” and “Phonology, Morphology and Word Segmentation”.

rai:personalSensitiveInformation.evidence: the S2AG Graph API offers general information such as metadata, authors, and citations

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We present ACL OCL, a scholarly corpus derived from the ACL Anthology to assist Open scientific research in the Computational Linguistics domain... Building scholarly corpora for open research accelerates scientific progress and promotes reproducibility in research... The structured full texts, enriched metadata from Semantic Scholar Academic Graph, and figures provided by OCL can benefit existing research tasks as well as enable more opportunities.

rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan.evidence: In the future, we will work on the data currency of OCL, which aims to keep OCL up-to-date with the ACL Anthology data. We plan to update OCL by year to keep it alive. The ultimate solution is to provide full-text extraction and information extraction APIs to ACL Anthology, thus hosting the OCL data on ACL Anthology itself.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: “we design crawlers to fetch all the PDF documents and metadata from its website... We remove PDF files longer than 50 pages” ; “we use GROBID for the full-text extraction from PDF files” ; “We take the S2ORC-JSON format... for our full-text schema” ; “To detect the language in which a document is written, we utilize a public language detection toolkit... with its title and abstract as inputs.”
